<Heading
  as={"h1"}
  className={"openapi__heading"}
  children={"Exchange OAuth token for a WordPress JWT (POST)"}
>
</Heading>

<MethodEndpoint
  method={"post"}
  path={"/oauth/token"}
  context={"endpoint"}
>
  
</MethodEndpoint>



API flow: exchanges a provider-issued token for a WordPress JWT and returns the
WordPress user profile. Use this variant for programmatic API clients. The provider
must be enabled in the plugin settings.

Supported providers: `google`, `auth0`, `facebook`, `github`.

**Google** - supply `code` (authorization code) or `id_token` (Google Sign-In ID
token). The `id_token` path returns a WordPress JWT directly; the `code` path
returns the raw Google token response for the client to handle. The `id_token` must
be issued for the configured client ID (unless "Allow tokens issued for other Google
clients" is enabled in the Google settings) and carry a verified email.

**Auth0** - supply `code` (returns the raw Auth0 token response) or `access_token`
(returns a WordPress JWT). The `access_token` must be a JWT issued for the configured
Auth0 Client ID (`azp` or `aud`). Opaque access tokens are rejected (error code 79)
unless "Allow opaque access tokens" is enabled in the Auth0 settings.
The account email must be verified.

The `code` flow sends the provider the "exchange code" Redirect URI saved in the
provider settings, so the code must have been issued for that URI.

**Facebook** - supply `access_token` (Facebook user access token). Returns a
WordPress JWT. The token must have been issued for the configured Facebook app
(checked with `debug_token`), and the App ID and App Secret must be set, unless
"Allow tokens issued for other Facebook apps" is enabled in the Facebook settings.

**GitHub** - supply `access_token` (GitHub user access token). Returns a
WordPress JWT. The token must have been issued for the configured GitHub OAuth
app (personal access tokens are rejected), and the Client ID and Client Secret
must be set, unless "Allow tokens issued for other GitHub apps" is enabled in the
GitHub settings.

If the OAuth identity matches an existing WordPress user (by email), a WordPress
JWT is returned. If no match is found and "Register on OAuth login" is enabled, a
new user is created automatically.
